w: In the evening assembly balaks and kishores presented a drama on the qualities of a bonafide sadhu.

In the evening assembly the Akshar Purushottam hostel students presented a lively kawali program. A sadhu, with reference to the program, said to Swamishri, "The presentation of the kawali was very good." "The drama (Ten Fools) was also well enacted," another sadhu added. "Swamishri, you were not looking. You were engaged in letter-writing," a sadhu said. "I saw it all. I was looking at it while writing letters. It is your ignorance that you were unable to understand this," Swamishri replied. " Because you were writing letters this thought came to me," the sadhu hesitantly said. "Did I not talk about the kawali and drama in my discourse," Swamishri responded. And then added, "If one perceives with the eye of knowledge and one's atma, then no such questions will arise as to whether he has seen it or not. He sees all." Like Bhagatji Maharaj who said, "A gnani (one who has realised knowledge) has infinite eyes." Swamishri sees everything even though he may not seem so.
A young boy, Vikesh, pointing at the murti of Shriji Maharaj, said to Swamishri, "That is your reflection."

Swamishri corrected him, "God is not our reflection but (pointing towards himself) we are His reflection. Because of Him we are great and glorious. Our powers have been given by Him. Everything is His. Remember, God is the highest and we should never forget Him."
Swamishri lucidly emphasized the supremity of Shriji Maharaj.
Study Well and Offer Devotion .
As part of Kishore Day celebration, 376 kishores and 750 kishoris pilgrimaged on foot from various suburbs to the mandir for Swamishri's morning puja.

The evening Kishore Day program included an impressive drama that showed how two modern teenagers who believed that the materialistic joys are the true objective of life and faith in God, mandirs and observing niyams are shackles that bind the individual were transformed through the presentation of two satsangi kishores. Prior to Swamishri's blessings, a torch-dance was performed by kishores.
For the last three years members of the Amdavad Kishore Mandal have been performing a fast a day for Swamishri's good health.

Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly, saying, "I was very pleased to see the Kishore Mandal's program. The program was such that it would have pleased Yogiji Maharaj immensely. Yogiji Maharaj used to like such talks and insisted upon what you showed, namely, the consolidation of moral commands in one's life, the strength of Satsang and the spirit to please God and His holy Sadhu."

On meeting Swamishri, Mr. Mandal, Zonal Executive director of ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Company), Ankleshwar, asked, "Despite all facilities for and payment of proper wages to laborers and office staff, why do they still talk of taking more rather than giving for what they get? And for this they create agitation. Why is this?"

Swamishri replied, "It is because of the rise in materialism we find such tendencies. Our culture teaches us to give. Our scriptures say that we should do something for others. They show the principles of charity, compassion, nonviolence, celibacy, etc. But we do not see this. People do not think as to what they should do for our society and country. But they entertain thoughts about doing things for themselves. And that is why we have conflicts. This is the reason for the lack of peace. What is required in education is not given (values). Firstly, it is the duty of parents, but they are not paying any attention. They have become busy. Along with education, spiritual education needs to be taught. Before we were taught poems like, 'O God, may we worship You ...' People talk about Ram's kingdom (Ram Rajya) today, but they do not think about how Ram ruled his kingdom. He did so much for his people.

"Maharaja Bhagwatsinhji of Gondal provided the needs of his citizens. He helped them in times of famine and calamities. He made such milestones that people could rest and get shade beneath it. He took care of such small needs of his people. He had his children educated and then told them to work as employees, and to make do with the salary provided. He believed that people's money should not be wasted. He lived in simplicity - clothes, food and everything. We should have such rulers; only then can the citizens live happily."

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.

Swamishri concluded his stay in Chicago by installing the murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni in the lower level of the mandir. Swamishri performed the first abhishek himself with water from the sacred rivers of India, after which senior sadhus and devotees did the same. After spending three months in North America, today Swamishri was to leave for London. In his final blessings to the devotees, he said that if one is unable to visit pilgrim places in India, one should not worry because the Chicago mandir is a pilgrim place for aspirants. He also explained that one who possesses true intelligence recognises God and His holy Sadhu. As devotees bid farewell to Swamishri, they knew that Swamishri's divine presence would always remain with them as he continues his vicharan to the United Kingdom, Africa, and finally back to India.
Chicago Mandir Murtis
Chicago Mandir Moods

Swamishri concluded his stay in Chicago by installing the murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni in the lower level of the Mandir. This golden murti rests atop a golden lotus, and allows countless devotees to offer an "abhishek", or bathe the murti with water. Swamishri performed the first abhishek himself with water from the sacred rivers of India, after which senior saints and devotees did the same.

Now, after a mere three months, Swamishri has taken Satsang to a new level in North America. His tireless efforts have enhanced the personal Satsang of thousands, and Satsang mandals as a whole in every major center he visited.
Swamishri's efforts also inspired children, teens, and youths to attend a national convention in Orlando, Florida where they learned about Indian culture and the ways of spiritualism.

He broke his own records by inaugurating two shikarbadh mandirs, what many claim as wonders of the world, in Houston and Chicago within a span of just 16 days. He performed the bhoomi pujan for Akshardham, a beautiful monument to be built with unique exhibitions illustrating India's religious history, in the state of New Jersey. In addition, he performed the Shilanyas Vidhi for shikarbadh mandirs to be built in Atlanta, Los Angeles, and Toronto. Though his accomplishments are endless, he remains humble in front of God and His devotees. He has revitalized Satsang and inspired higher ideals in existing and new aspirants.

In his final blessings to the devotees, he said that if one is unable to visit pilgrimage places in India, one should not worry because the Chicago Mandir is a pilgrimage place for aspirants. He also explained that one who possesses a true buddhi recognizes God and His Saint. Most importantly, he elaborated on how devotees receive many in return if they give only a little to God.

As devotees bid farewell to Swamishri, they knew that Swamishri's divine presence would always remain with them though he continues his vicharan to the United Kingdom, Africa, and finally back to India.

A doctor phoned from America. For many years he has been taking the examination for residency, but he does not pass. Today too he asked for blessings, and Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "We will certainly pray, but everyone in the world passes, so why do you not? Think about the reason for that."
Today India's famous actor Amitabh Bachchan had darshan of Bhagwan Swaminarayan at Swaminarayan Akshardham in Gandhinagar and thoroughly enjoyed the 'Sat Chit Anand' water show.

Impressed by the Sat Chit Anand water show, he spoke with Pramukh Swami Maharaj on the phone and said, "Please accept my pranams. I saw the programme here and was very pleased. I seek your blessings." Swamishri gave him blessings.

In the visitors' book too, describing his experience, he had written, "I have had darshan of Akshardham many times, but what I experienced today brought peace to my mind. I truly understood the meaning of atma and Paramatma. I thank this mandir and all its swamis and volunteers from my heart, and I hope that the Lord's grace always remains on all of you."
That same night, on his blog on the internet, he put his experience of Akshardham into words like this:

"Today the day ended with another wonderful and amazing moment. That moment was a visit to the Akshardham mandir in Gandhinagar, the capital of Gujarat, 20 minutes from Ahmedabad. The Akshardham mandirs in different parts of the country are astonishing achievements of architecture, and the mandir in Gandhinagar is in no way inferior. The construction and design are original, and it has been built without the use of iron. The Akshardham mandirs are spotlessly clean and preserve their natural beauty. As a result, one experiences holiness here. A team of very dedicated, sincere and hardworking sadhus and volunteers runs it and teaches everyone its principles and beliefs.

Tonight the mandir was kept open late for me, and in that there was boundless grace. After the darshan and visit to the mandir, in the vast premises of the mandir, we came to see what we had gone for, the 'laser cum water show', full of research and teaching. I must say, 'I have never seen such wonderful work anywhere before.'

In an amphitheatre with a capacity of 2,500 people, set in a lovely open space, we watched a dramatic, wonderful water show that delighted the mind, presenting the philosophy of Akshardham in the form of a symbolic story. It was a real joy to watch the story of Nachiketa, the son of a rishi, and Yamraj, the god of death, with scenes brought to life by laser beams on the flowing fountains. The deep secret of atma and Paramatma was woven so beautifully and wonderfully into the episodes shown on the varied water screen that I began to feel proud that my close friend J. J. Bhatt had invited me to watch this wonderful programme. Such an experience of fulfilment, and after that being able to have a short conversation on the phone with Pramukh Swamiji, whom I have met many times to receive his blessings, was the ideal and best conclusion to today's events. How can I put it into words! That time was out of this world!"

At the shibir, as at every centre, there was the "Iti Vachanamrutam" programme here today. The presenter and the listeners took their places before Mahant Swami Maharaj. The presenter began the reading: "Swaminarayan Hare, Vachanamrut Houston section 1." Then, arranged in the style of the Vachanamrut's descriptions, the listeners one by one held questions and answers with Swamishri. Let us enjoy those questions and answers:
Question: We cannot sit cross legged even for five minutes, so how will we ever master ashtang yoga (the eightfold path of yoga)?
Swamishri said, "Having met Shriji Maharaj and Swami, and having met Pramukh Swami Maharaj, is greater than ashtang yoga."
Everyone burst out laughing and clapped.

Question: Here too a short skit was presented, in which a call for seva was made during an assembly and many people stood up, including the presenter. Swamishri was told, "Swami! This is how it is with us and katha, so please explain the true glory of katha."

Answering, Swamishri said, "Once Yogi Bapa was giving a discourse in the assembly. At that time a call for seva came. Those who thought they were free stood up. But if the seva can be put off, then one should listen to the katha. Swami said in his talks that one who does seva and also learns knowledge keeps growing. One who does only one of the two does not grow. And one who does neither declines. But if the seva is urgent, one has to go. For example, once Yogi Bapa was doing puja in the Akshar Deri. Shambhusinh began the kirtan, 'Prat thayu manmohan pyara...' (It is dawn, my beloved enchanter). Yogi Bapa said, 'Go, Shambhusinh! Go and drain the water from the banana plantation. Sing "it is dawn" there.' So we have to use discretion. Because Yogi Bapa said so, he went, but basically both are needed, katha and seva."
Question: How did you understand Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj? Please write it for us.
Swamishri wrote: "Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj are the very manifest form of Shriji Maharaj."

Question: We do not know what to do in satsang. Giving a portion of income, discussions, seva, para sabha, ghar sabha and the niyams of Chaturmas: we have to do all of this. How much can we do? Please tell us one spiritual practice that, if we do it, everything else will come automatically.

Swamishri said, "See divinity in everyone. And Yogi Bapa and Shriji Maharaj have said, 'The sadhus and devotees are divine. One who understands, holds and reflects on this deep secret becomes absorbed in bliss. His joy does not fade at any time of the day.' But divinity in everyone. This is hard, but this is the only way... the key to Akshardham."

In a skit, a spiritual seeker was shown searching for the four forms of Akshardham. Another seeker said, "Brother! Not the four forms of Akshardham, the four forms of Akshar." Saying this, he counted three, but even he could not find the fourth form.
The real aim was to have Swamishri say it with his own lips, so Swamishri was requested, "Swami! Please tell us yourself what the fourth form is."
Swamishri burst out laughing and said, "You will not get an answer."
Everyone roared with laughter. Immediately the question was changed and Swamishri was asked, "You are the fourth form of Akshardham, aren't you?"
This time Swamishri smiled and said, "What you understand is right." Again there was laughter.

Another short skit was presented, in which a volunteer said, "My letter was never reaching Mahant Swami Maharaj. When I looked, there was no stamp on it at all." From this, Swamishri was told, "Swami! We are all like letters without stamps. In every birth our letter comes back to earth. Our true address is really Akshardham. But our letter does not reach there. So in this very birth, we will get the stamp for Akshardham, won't we?"
Giving his assurance, Swamishri said, "You will. If you want to stick it on!" Then he said, "The stamp is firm conviction in Bhagwan and keeping niyams."

st.t: US Congressmen Ed Case and Rich McCormick Deepen Cultural Exchange Through Enriching Visit
w: US Congressmen Ed Case (HI-1) and Rich McCormick (GA-6) recently visited the Swaminarayan Akshardham complex in New Delhi.

After a traditional welcome, the congressmen and their delegation explored the architecture of and paid respects at the Akshardham Mandir. The delegation also performed abhishek of the murti of Shri Neelkanth Varni to pray for world peace and harmony.
They also experienced the cultural boat ride depicting India’s rich heritage and the breathtaking Sahaj Anand Water Show that has garnered global acclaim.

The visit helped the delegation to gain profound insights into the spiritual, artistic, and historical significance that Akshardham embodies, promoting a deeper understanding of India’s diverse cultural tapestry.

Congressman Ed Case stated, “Exploring Akshardham has been a captivating journey. Its architecture and cultural representations provide an insightful window into India’s rich heritage that is truly inspiring.”

Congressman Rich McCormick said, “The visit exemplified the transformative power of cultural exchange in fostering mutual understanding and appreciation. Akshardham stands as a compelling testament to India’s cultural richness.”
